Stop lying to the Greeks life without the euro is great

The author of this piece should stop fooling himself. Greece is not Iceland, Sweden, or Romania. Their problems run much deeper than anything the aforementioned countries have ever faced. The European banks have basically written Greece off as a total loss and are making an example out of them since showing leniency would set a precedent for Spain, Italy, and every other financially troubled European country to demand handouts the central bank can't afford to give.

The future is bleak. Voting no to the EU all but guarantees an exit from the Eurozone. Greece will have no choice but to reissue the Drachma. And unfortunately, the history of the Weimar Republic and Zimbabwe proved that switching to a new currency in the midst of crisis often leads to hyperinflation + an even worse economic collapse.

I think you're missing the point, which is that Greece has already collapsed economically. Staying in the euro won't help a bit, especially with the demand from the ECB that Greece be used as a conduit to bail-out the banks elsewhere in Europe (already happened).

The only thing Greece risks with a new currency is financial warfare from the large powers who wish to see it fail. Fundamentally, they're otherwise well prepared. Billionaires agree with you, everyone else knows that if you have food production and sources of foreign/hard currency (tourism is a good one, and Greece kind of excels there) you can easily make a go of it on your own.

Regarding the last statement, about German bonds, hell yeah he's right. German banks are some of the idiots who LOANED Greece the money you say it's so obvious they can't pay back. What does that say about them???

Personally, I think Greece should leave the Euro too. All the financial aid + emergency loans that went to Greece since 2010 has been wasted, including a 100 billion Euro debt write-off in 2012. The more I read about it, the more it sounds like pumping money into a sinking ship. If someone screwed up their personal finances as badly as the Greeks did, the banks would have long since written off the debt and sold it to a collections agency.

Speaking of banks, if someone takes a loan out on a 5 million dollar house when they have an annual income of 50 thousand dollars a year, they're fucking stupid and deserve to take a financial hit for their stupidity. Normally, the bank deserves blame too for reckless lending, however, the Greek government rigged the system by cooking their economic books. In 2009, the Greek government claimed their deficit spending was 6%–8% of GDP when in reality, their deficit spending rate was at 15%! I have a hard time blaming the Germans for loaning money to someone when they've been falsifying their paperwork as long and as successfully as the Greeks did.

If Greece can pull off a miraculous recovery, then more power to them. But I'm not holding my breath, and I'm sure most foreign investors aren't either.
